safetyPlanPage.heading: Make A Safety Plan
safetyPlanPage.intro: Build a personalized safety plan step by step, together with the client, to help them stay safe through moments of suicidal ideation. Each step focuses on one part of the plan — add as many items as apply, then review the whole plan before printing a copy for the client to keep.
safetyPlanPage.crisisBanner: If you or someone you know is in immediate danger, call 911. You can also call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, available 24/7.
safetyPlanPage.disclaimer: This tool is a starting point for completing the Stanley-Brown Safety Planning Intervention together with a client. It saves only in this browser — nothing is sent anywhere.

steps.heading: My Warning Signs
steps.intro: A warning sign is something the client thinks, feels, or does as suicidal thoughts are starting to develop.
steps.placeholder: e.g. trouble sleeping, pulling away from friends

steps.heading: My Coping Strategies
steps.intro: Coping strategies are things the client can do on their own to feel a little better in the moment, without needing to contact anyone else.
steps.placeholder: e.g. listen to music, go for a walk, draw

steps.heading: My Distractions
steps.intro: Distractions are people or places that may offer comfort or help the client take a break from the situation, so they can start feeling or thinking differently.
steps.placeholder: e.g. a friend's house, the school gym

steps.heading: My Supports
steps.intro: Supports are people the client feels comfortable talking to about what they're going through, and who can help. When possible, it helps to talk with them about being a support before a crisis happens.
steps.placeholder: e.g. a parent, sibling, coach, or friend

steps.heading: My Professional Supports
steps.intro: Professional contacts are people who can provide professional care and support, including therapists, doctors, and crisis lines.
steps.placeholder: e.g. therapist name and phone number

steps.heading: My Safer Environment
steps.intro: Having items nearby that could be used for self-harm can be dangerous during a crisis. What items might need to be stored safely, given to someone else, or removed — and how?
steps.placeholder: e.g. ask a parent to store medications

safetyPlanPage.stepHint: Add as many or as few as apply — you can leave it blank and move on if it isn't relevant yet.
safetyPlanPage.reviewIntro: Here's the full plan from what was entered. Add, remove, or adjust anything before printing.
safetyPlanPage.downloadHint: Opens your browser's print dialog — choose “Save as PDF” as the destination to download it.
safetyPlanPage.emptyStateText: Nothing entered yet — fill in at least one step to download or print the plan.
